title: Matrices, linear maps and adjoints
objectives: Interpret matrix columns as transformed basis vectors.
Track composition order and dimensions; calculate adjoints.
prerequisites: Chapter 2’s vectors, basis labels and matrix multiplication; elementary algebra. New notation is developed in the text.

quizzes.question: A acts first, followed by B. Which matrix describes the composition?
feedback: The rightmost matrix acts first on a column.
Addition combines outputs, not successive operations.

quizzes.question: Is every Hermitian matrix unitary?
options: No; diag(1,2) is Hermitian but not unitary.
Only when its entries are real.
feedback: Hermitian and unitary are different conditions.
Correct. Its adjoint product is diag(1,4), not identity.
Being real does not enforce norm preservation.
